claims.statement: A 2025 Polish Justice Ministry consultation document describes guarantee retentions as common in construction, often deducted from monthly compensation and sometimes held for up to five years.
GDDKiA guidance for subcontractor direct-payment requests requires acceptance without reservations and documentary proof, showing that release depends on a structured evidence packet in public works.
Under eIDAS, an electronic signature cannot be denied legal effect solely because it is electronic, and a qualified electronic signature has the equivalent legal effect of a handwritten signature.

contrary_evidence: Retention terms are contract-specific and a digital evidence vault does not resolve insolvency, bad-faith withholding, or genuine defects.
Document-management and construction ERP products may already cover part of the closeout workflow.

economics.acquisition_route: Begin with a construction lawyer or guarantee broker that can bring a small portfolio of active retentions
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 6-8 year path would require approximately 1,500-2,000 active projects at about 4,000 PLN average annual recurring revenue, partner-led acquisition, and a valuable contract/outcome dataset while the founder retains material ownership
economics.founder_time: Approximately 10-14 hours per week with legal interpretation and dispute advice explicitly outsourced
economics.gross_margin_basis: Workflow software and automated contract extraction less qualified-signature, storage, and specialist review costs
economics.payback: One timely retention tranche or avoided evidence reconstruction can exceed annual fees, but willingness to pay before a dispute is uncertain
economics.pricing: Roughly 2,500 PLN project onboarding plus 300-600 PLN per active project month, with optional release-packet fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Projects remain active throughout delivery and warranty periods, and contractors start new projects repeatedly

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A clause and outcome library could identify recurring release blockers, improve contract setup, and create reliable counterparty process histories
fingerprint.customer: Polish construction subcontractors, general contractors, project SPVs, and guarantee or receivables-finance providers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Distribute through subcontractor accountants, construction-law firms, guarantee brokers, industry associations, and public-project consultants
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Contract extraction, milestone calendar, e-sign acceptance, defect notice workflow, evidence vault, and lender- or court-ready export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A contractor, subcontractor consortium, or finance partner pays per project and per year; a completion fee applies when a release-ready tranche receipt is countersigned
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Work is accepted but part of compensation remains retained for years and the parties disagree or lose track of defects, notices, warranty dates, or release documentation

founder_fit: The workflow rewards structured evidence, automation, and quantitative ageing analysis
It can be tested on historical project files without founder camera exposure
Partner distribution can reduce the need for constant direct networking
risks: The platform cannot compel a reluctant counterparty to release money
Legal advice boundaries and professional liability must be explicit
General contractors may resist a tool that increases release transparency
Construction documents are inconsistent and may require expensive review

structure.commercial_archetype: Per-project closeout and retention evidence vault
structure.control_point: The counterparty-signed acceptance clock and complete defect-and-remedy record that supports each retention-release tranche
structure.critical_dependency: General contractors must participate and contracts must recognise the digital acceptance and notice trail as valid evidence

thesis: Polish construction subcontractors and general contractors could share a project-specific retention passport that extracts release conditions from the contract, records signed partial and final acceptance, tracks defects and warranty clocks, and produces a release-ready evidence packet. It would not force payment or hold funds; it would make the exact contractual release event and unresolved exceptions visible to both sides and to financing or guarantee partners.
title: Retention Release Passport
uncertainties: Average administrative cost and delayed amount per SME subcontractor
Whether the buyer is the subcontractor, general contractor, lender, or guarantee broker
Which signature and notice methods typical contracts accept
How often missing evidence rather than insolvency or substantive defects causes delayed release
